blocks.html:
Shared vocabulary used across these books. Terms scoped to one stack are marked (legacy) or (k8s).

Core concepts

Deploy App The self-hosted system that provides a single secure login and identity flow across several mission-critical services, with new services added via integration APIs. Codenamed RASENMAEHER.

RASENMAEHER The project codename for Deploy App (an infantry joke; German for "lawnmower"). Used interchangeably with "Deploy App" in the codebase and these docs.

rmapi (core) The core RASENMAEHER API — the rmapi service/container running the rasenmaeher_api application from pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api. It owns main user CRUD and the Deploy App operations and is the point of integration that product integrations call. The thing an integrator builds is never called "rmapi".

Product integration API (product-rm integration API) The service you build to integrate a product into Deploy App. It registers with / is driven by the core rmapi, which calls its user-lifecycle endpoints (create/promote/demote/delete) over mTLS. Examples: python-matrix-rmapi, python-tak-rmapi, python-mediamtx-rmmtxauthz. Scaffolded from python-integration-template.

EUD End User Device — a phone, tablet, or laptop a user runs the product client on (for example ATAK/WinTAK/iTAK after downloading a client package from Deploy App).

mTLS Mutual TLS: both client and server present certificates. Deploy App uses it for service-to-service trust, including the core rmapi's callbacks to product integration APIs (the caller's certificate CN must match the RASENMAEHER service certificate).

Identity and components

Keycloak The identity provider behind the shared single login flow. On legacy it sits on the kc. subdomain; on Kubernetes it is managed by the keycloak-operator.

Legacy stack (Docker Compose)

miniwerk (legacy) pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-miniwerk. Handles Let's Encrypt certificate issuance, the subdomain scheme, and the MW_PRODUCTS product list for the compose stack. Does not exist on Kubernetes.

MW_PRODUCTS (legacy) The miniwerk environment variable listing which products are part of the deployment (e.g. tak,kc,fake,bl,mtx,matrix,synapse). Adding a product means adding its short name here so its subdomains and routing are provisioned.

CFSSL (legacy) pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-cfssl. The internal certificate authority for the legacy stack. Replaced on Kubernetes by cert-manager / trust-manager / opendefense-pki.

Kubernetes stack (opendefence-platform)

⚠️ Closed alpha. OpenDefence on Kubernetes (opendefence-platform) is in closed alpha, under rapid and breaking development, and will most likely be superseded by the documentation that ships with the first public release. Treat the Kubernetes content here as provisional — not a production target.

cert-manager (k8s) The Kubernetes controller that issues and renews certificates. Replaces CFSSL's issuing role.

trust-manager (k8s) Distributes the CA trust bundle across the cluster so workloads trust the internal CA.

opendefense-pki (k8s) The in-cluster PKI definition (root and intermediate CA / issuers) that backs internal mTLS. Replaces CFSSL as the CA source.

Kustomize (k8s) The templating-free Kubernetes config tool used to build manifests. Each app is split into base/ (environment-agnostic) and overlays/<env>/ (environment-specific).

overlay (k8s) An overlays/<env>/ directory that customizes a base/ for a specific environment — image registries, hostnames, certificates, and ingress. The repo ships local and cloud overlays.

kind (k8s) Kubernetes IN Docker — runs a local Kubernetes cluster inside Docker for development (task up creates one). Pinned to 0.31 via mise.

k3s (k8s) A lightweight Kubernetes distribution used for external/cloud clusters (for example a Zarf deploy targets a k3s cluster via its KUBECONFIG).

mise (k8s) The tool-version manager that pins the exact versions of helm, kind, kubectl, task, yq, and zarf. Run mise install to get them and mise trust to trust local config.

task (Taskfile) (k8s) The task runner (taskfile.dev) used as the default command interface: task up, task down, task deploy, and so on. Tasks include ordered readiness gates between deploy phases.

Zarf (k8s) A packaging/airgap-friendly tool used to build a deployable package from the cloud overlays (task zarf:package:cloud) and deploy it to an external cluster.

Traefik (k8s) The ingress controller / reverse proxy on the Kubernetes stack. Replaces nginx (which on legacy is driven by miniwerk).
